scope: READ_ONLY_INDEPENDENT_PROVIDER_RECORD_METADATA_AND_CHECKSUM_AUDIT; NEVER DOWNLOAD BENCHMARK DATA OR EXECUTE SCIENTIFIC CASE
questions: Does the Zenodo provider's exact record ID exist, match the claimed version, publisher, release, and license?
Does the record expose immutable per-file names, sizes, checksums, and direct download links without needing to retrieve dataset bytes?
Does the published code/Zenodo record give enough evidence to assert correct paired shared-noise counterfactuals? (Metadata alone must NOT)
Can an independent provider-side record be bound to an independently retained source-frozen manifest, without equating a publisher-supplied checksum to physical independent first-use?

data_acquisition_policy.may_read: Zenodo DOI page, api/records/23095083 metadata JSON, independently published code tree, provider's manifest listing names/checksums only if tiny/authorized by source-only contract
data_acquisition_policy.must_not: download Parquet, TAR/ZIP, executable dataset archive, model rows, original protected scientific cases, replay consumed seeds, hidden SCM labels, CHECK or holdout
data_acquisition_policy.provider_checksum: Record as provider-claimed checksum algorithm and value, not verified bytes; SHA256 if absent must remain unknown

strict_identity.reject_if_malformed: no invented missing metadata, checksum, temporal pairing, license or source authority

source_eligibility.exact_model_input_allowlist_from_H: unchanged; do not weaken model-data separation

planned_outputs: immutable provider readback structured manifest, with provider URLs and checksums as claimed
targeted stdlib metadata validator and adversarial focused tests
negative or partial outcome logged with verified local/GitHub bytes
next blocking conditions documented; no original science admission
